one-check-per-line.why: all 6 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 6

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 6 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why: The verifier brief's Check 1 is stricter than its expect line. Its PASS condition requires the bad file to print "exactly two stdout lines". The expect line only says the tool "prints <file>:<line>: <error> for every row that is not valid JSON". It never says the lines go to stdout, and it doesn't rule out other output such as a summary line. A tool that wrote the error lines to stderr, or added a "2 errors" line, would meet the words but fail this check. That extra rule belongs under Advisory. Checks 2, 3 and 5 match their words. Checks 4 and 6 are close: they add things like running npm ci and requiring the workspace tests to pass, which the words arguably imply. The Advisory section correctly holds the CRLF, lockfile and shebang checks. Because Check 1 breaks the criterion, it doesn't hold for the whole output.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs. Builder: `chmod +x` / `git update-index --chmod=+x`, `npm install`, `npm ci && npm test` and `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js` all target files that earlier steps create. Verifier: the `printf` fixtures have no stray `%`. Check 3's `node --input-type=module -e "import { lint } from './packages/...'..."` quotes correctly in bash: `\"` becomes `"` and `\n` reaches JS as a newline escape, and a relative import from eval resolves against the working directory. Check 4's `node -e "const p=require(...)"` is valid CommonJS eval. `npm test -w jsonl-lint` matches the workspace name. The `gh pr view/checks/list` flags are valid. `test -s` and `grep -n` are fine. Two small gaps: `<PR>` is a placeholder the verifier must fill in, and `$T` stands for the temp dir it creates first but is never assigned. Neither breaks syntax or names a file that doesn't exist.

catches-traps.why: Item 1 is met: builder step 7 says "Run `npm install` at the repo root to update `package-lock.json`" and step 8 commits it. Item 2 is met: step 6 says "replace the 'No tools yet' bullet". Item 4 is met: Check 6 reads the PR body and headRefOid with gh, and PASS requires the test workflow run "for the head commit concluded success". Item 3 is missing. Check 4 runs `npm test -w jsonl-lint` directly in the workspace. Check 6 only checks that the root `npm ci && npm test` exits 0. Nothing in the verifier brief reads the test count from the root `npm test` output or breaks `lint()` to see a test fail. So the brief would not notice the root script's `--if-present` silently skipping the jsonl-lint tests.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked every verifier PASS/FAIL condition against its line, and the builder steps too. Nothing is stricter than its line. Check 1 asks for `<file>:<line>: ` followed by "a non-empty error text", not exact error wording. Check 2 only asks for non-empty stderr and exit 2. Check 4 allows "extra args only if it still runs node --test". Check 6 only asks for one PR, the Closes text and green checks. No brief sets a branch-name rule, a mutation test or a limit on which files the PR may touch. CRLF handling and the executable bit are under Advisory as "notes, not failures". Every behaviour line is checked by running something: the CLI on printf fixtures (Checks 1–2), importing `lint` (Check 3), `npm test -w jsonl-lint` (Check 4), and `npm ci && npm test` plus `gh pr checks` (Check 6). Reading files is only used for structure lines (package.json fields, test case coverage, READMEs), and Check 4 runs the tests as well.

methods-private.why: The criterion holds. I compared the builder brief with each verifier check. The builder brief has no PASS or FAIL conditions. It also leaves out every verifier probe: the exact `printf` fixtures (e.g. `bad.jsonl` with line 4 bad and line 6 torn), the Check 3 inline `node --input-type=module -e "import { lint }..."` script, the Check 4 `node -e require(package.json)` script, and the `gh pr view`/`gh pr checks`/`gh pr list` commands. What the builder gets is implementation guidance, plus the allowed items: write its own node:test tests, run `npm ci && npm test` (expect line 6 names npm test), and wait for the test workflow to pass. Step 7 asks for a hand run of the CLI on a clean file, a bad file, a missing file and no argument. That is generic self-testing with no fixed inputs or expected outputs, so it does not reuse a verifier probe.
